# montecarlo_sql_server_credentials (Resource)

SQL Server credentials are the login Monte Carlo stores for SQL Server connections to use: a SQL login, or Windows Authentication with Kerberos. The password and the keytab are never returned.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `host` (String) Hostname of the database endpoint. For `kerberos`, the fully qualified name the server's service principal is registered under.
- `port` (Number) Port the database listens on.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `auth_mode` (String) How Monte Carlo signs in. `sql` takes `user` and `password`. `kerberos` takes `realm`, `kdc`, `principal`, and one of `keytab_base64` or `password`.
- `db_name` (String) Database to connect to.
- `kdc` (String) Hostname of the key distribution center, optionally with `:port`, for `kerberos`.
- `keytab_base64_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Base64-encoded keytab for `principal`, for `kerberos`. Send this or `password`. Stored by Monte Carlo and never returned.
- `keytab_base64_wo_version` (Number) Bump to send `keytab_base64_wo` again. Terraform stores this, never the secret.
- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Password of `user` for `sql`, or of the Active Directory account behind `principal` for `kerberos`. Stored by Monte Carlo and never returned.
- `password_wo_version` (Number) Bump to send `password_wo` again. Terraform stores this, never the secret.
- `principal` (String) Active Directory principal Monte Carlo signs in as, for `kerberos`.
- `realm` (String) Kerberos realm, normally the Active Directory domain in capitals, for `kerberos`.
- `user` (String) SQL login Monte Carlo signs in as, for `sql`.

### Read-Only

- `connection_type` (String) The connection type the credentials are for, such as `snowflake`. Fixed once created.
- `created_time` (String) When the credentials were created.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the credentials.
- `storage_type` (String) Where the secret lives. Fixed once created.
